summary: Full-extraction pass on Lithuania's whistleblower law (XIII-804), its Government implementing resolution 1133, three Competition Council news releases on cartel-informant rewards and the Prosecutor's Office 2023 and 2024 activity reports. Added procedural rules for both reward schemes and the Prosecutor's Office whistleblower statistics (reports, status decisions, pre-trial investigations, retaliation and compensation requests, legal aid, money identified) under a proposed protection-only programme ltu-gp-wb.

events.title: Lithuania adopts the Law on the Protection of Whistleblowers (rewards for valuable information)
events.description: The Seimas adopts Law No. XIII-804 on the Protection of Whistleblowers: the Prosecutor's Office becomes the competent institution; recognised whistleblowers may receive a reward for valuable information (Art. 12, no maximum, not tied to a court judgment) and compensation of up to 50 basic social benefits (Art. 13), plus free legal aid and confidentiality. In force 1 January 2019.
events.location: PDF p. 1 and Art. 18(1), PDF p. 10

events.title: Lithuanian whistleblower law and rewards for valuable information take effect
events.description: Law XIII-804 on the Protection of Whistleblowers enters into force, making rewards for valuable information available through the Prosecutor's Office.
events.quote: Šis įstatymas įsigalioja 2019 m. sausio 1 d.

events.title: Lithuanian Government sets the procedure for whistleblower rewards and compensation
events.description: Government Resolution No. 1133 approves the procedure for rewarding whistleblowers for valuable information (one-off payment decided by the Prosecutor General on a commission's proposal within three months, paid within one month, net of taxes, from the Prosecutor General's Office budget), the compensation procedure and the rules for internal reporting channels (mandatory in public bodies and in organisations with 50 or more employees). In force 1 January 2019.
events.quote: Šis nutarimas įsigalioja 2019 m. sausio 1 dieną.

events.title: Lithuanian Competition Council offers rewards for evidence in ongoing dairy and coffee-machine investigations
events.description: The Competition Council invites people with information on its ongoing investigations (a suspected raw-milk purchase price cartel among dairy processors, and suspected resale price fixing of Jura coffee machines by distributor Rickman Trade) to come forward, saying evidence on investigations already under way may earn a reward of up to EUR 100,000.
events.quote: Individuals who submit evidence related to investigations already being conducted by our institution may also qualify for a reward.

events.title: Lithuanian Prosecutor's Office launches whistleblower website pranesktiesa.lt
events.description: A website for whistleblowers (who can become one, how to report, laws, forms, consultation line, examples of protection and reward measures) starts operating in September 2023.

ledger.contains: Law No. XIII-804 of 28 Nov 2017 on the Protection of Whistleblowers (10 pp., original text, in force 1 Jan 2019): definitions; grounds for reports; channels (internal, competent institution, public) with 5- and 2-working-day handling deadlines; Prosecutor's Office as competent institution and its functions incl. publishing statistics; recognition as whistleblower; confidentiality; ban on retaliation and reversed burden of proof; remedies; Art. 12 reward for valuable information (any violation, proportional to damage, no maximum, not tied to a court judgment, procedure set by Government); Art. 13 compensation up to 50 basic social benefits, not combined with a reward; Art. 14 free secondary legal aid; Art. 15 exemption from liability; Art. 16 internal channels. Anonymous reporters get protection only if their identity is revealed (Art. 3(6)); a report must give the name (Art. 4(6)). No statistics. Rules award_cap (none) and discretionary were already in the data; added conviction_required = 0 and compensation cap (proposed rules) and the adoption and entry-into-force events.

Government Resolution No. 1133 of 14 Nov 2018 (17 pp.), in force 1 Jan 2019, approving three procedures: (1) rewards for valuable information: one-off payment to recognised whistleblowers; conditions (valuable information that prevented or reduced damage, brought or saved funds, or helped prevent, stop or investigate a crime; no other payment for it); amount by reasonableness and proportionality; request form to the Prosecutor General's Office with name, birth date, contacts, account; commission of at least three members, extra data within at least 5 working days; decision within 3 months, notice within 5 working days, payment within 1 month net of taxes from the Prosecutor General's Office budget appropriations; repayment if knowingly false data; disputes under administrative procedure; (2) compensation for negative impact (same commission, 3-month decision, 1-month payment; no compensation if a reward was received or requested); (3) internal reporting channels (mandatory in public bodies and in entities with 50 or more employees; 2-working-day forwarding; 5-working-day reply; data kept at least 3 years) with report form. No statistics. Rules added: decision and payment deadlines, taxes deducted, no anonymous request; event for the resolution. Internal-channel and compensation procedure details are recorded here in words only.

Competition Council news release on the Seimas adopting amendments to the Law on Competition (14 Mar 2019; page last updated 27 Jun 2019): right to reward whistleblowers on anti-competitive agreements and protect their identity; single payment of 1% of fines, EUR 1,000-100,000; no reward for evidence obtained by a criminal offence or through law-enforcement duties (else repayable); also procedural fines, structural remedies and monitoring of public bodies from 1 July (out of scope). The adoption event was already in the data; added the rate, cap and minimum rows from this release.

Competition Council news release (28 Jun 2019) on approving its whistleblower remuneration procedure: rewards from 1 July 2019; 1% of fines, EUR 1,000-100,000; channels (e-mail, post, in person) and prior consultations; identity withheld from the parties on request; decision within 20 days of the official disclosure of the infringement; information must come before the decision to open an investigation and be lawfully obtained (else repayable); staff of a leniency applicant and officials with access through their duties excluded; paid from the authority's budget; cartel fines up to 10% of gross annual income and manager disqualification for 3-5 years plus a EUR 14,481 fine (out of scope). Launch event, rate and cap were already in the data; added the minimum, decision deadline and exclusion.

Competition Council news release (13 May 2026) inviting information on two ongoing investigations (dairy processors' raw-milk price cartel; Rickman Trade / Jura coffee machine price fixing); rewards up to EUR 100,000, also for evidence on investigations already under way; amount set by added value of the evidence, severity, duration and impact of the infringement, cooperation and risk taken; confidentiality; contact channels; context on fines up to 10% of turnover and leniency reductions up to 50% (out of scope). No statistics on rewards. Added the cap row (as of 2026) and a context event; the apparent widening to ongoing investigations is flagged in notes.

Prosecutor's Office activity report for 2023 (30 pp.): criminal prosecution, pre-trial investigation, court work, public-interest defence, staff and budget (out of scope). Section 12 (PDF p. 23-25) on whistleblower protection: 76 reports from 67 persons (+31% on 2022, 51); money identified in investigations opened on whistleblower information (nearly EUR 38 m unpaid taxes, about EUR 48 m other damage, civil claims nearly EUR 2.5 m, granted nearly EUR 71 thousand, EUR 317,672 paid to the budget; period not stated); status decisions pie (57% recognised, 43% not) and reasons; list of reported violation types; pre-trial investigations started/refused chart 2021-2023 (read from bar labels, series by colour); criminal-code articles; 8 retaliation complaints (2022: 10) and types; 3 reward requests (2022: 2), no reward granted (2022: 1) (already in the data); 3 compensation requests, none paid (words, no 0 row); legal aid to 5 whistleblowers (2022: 5); website launched Sept 2023; awareness (Delfi articles read by over 7,000; ads shown over 5.3 m times, 1.2 m unique users; forum, NEIWA) left out as not programme measures. Non-reward statistics filed under proposed programme ltu-gp-wb.

Prosecutor's Office activity report for 2024 (31 pp.): prosecution, pre-trial work, courts, public-interest defence, staff (table of prosecutors 2020-2024) and budget (out of scope). Section 12 (PDF p. 25-27): money identified 2020-2024 from investigations on whistleblower information (nearly EUR 38 m taxes, about EUR 48 m other damage, civil claims over EUR 3 m, granted over EUR 73 thousand, EUR 327,222 paid to the budget); 80 reports in 2024 (+5% on 76); status pie 50% recognised, 49% not, 1% left unexamined; violation types; pre-trial investigations started/refused chart 2022-2024 (bar labels, series by colour); 8 retaliation complaints (2023: 8); 3 reward requests (2023: 3): 2 returned unexamined for lack of status, 1 examined and refused (requests, refusal and no award already in the data); no compensation requests in 2024 (2023: 3; words, no 0 row); legal aid to 5 (2023: 5); 258 helpline consultations; awareness (8,205 training participants, Delfi ads over 2.3 m views and 665 thousand unique visitors, TV clip, bus, guidelines) left out as not programme measures. Non-reward statistics filed under proposed programme ltu-gp-wb. The 2022-2023 chart values match the 2023 report.
